extracted.intended_audience: Presbytery members, church leaders, and engaged laity in the Church of Scotland (readers concerned with covenantal reformation and ecclesiastical discipline)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards for judging the faithfulness, consistency, and lawfulness of a party's renewal of covenants, public prayers, testimony, terms of communion, and exercise of church discipline in the context of the covenanted Reformation. Applied to evaluate whether the 'Seceders' conduct conforms to the covenants and scriptural polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scriptural warrant for prayer
rubrics_metrics.description: Prayers (especially public national prayers) must have scripture warrant and be founded on the promises of God; one should not pray in faith for things contrary to Scripture or Christ's mediatory intercession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Praying for the preservation of civil/ ecclesiastical constitutions or limited royal successions that are contrary to God's word, while simultaneously praying for a revival of covenanted reformation. Example concern raised: praying that God preserve an Erastian government or a limited succession to the throne has 'no scripture warrant' and cannot be made in faith. Such prayers are contradictory and cannot be acceptable to God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency of prayers and professions
rubrics_metrics.description: A public profession (prayer or address) must be consistent in its parts; it must not assert the need for revival of reformation while simultaneously seeking preservation of institutions that obstruct reformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text highlights the contradiction of praying for the overthrow of mountains that hinder reformation while praying for the preservation of a constitution acknowledged to be 'a mighty bar' against reformation. Consistency is required between ends sought and the means prayed for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness to the covenants when professed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party professes the moral and perpetual obligation of the National Covenant and the Solemn League and Covenant, its principles, acts, and bonds must be consistent with the content and spirit of those covenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Claiming to renew the covenants while omitting their substance or adopting principles (e.g., approving prelatical government) expressly abjured by the covenants. The Presbytery judges such behavior as 'treachery' and 'burying' of the covenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of covenant renovation
rubrics_metrics.description: A genuine renovation of the National Covenant/Solemn League and Covenant must include the material clauses and articles of those covenants rather than omit or alter their essential parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete guidance: Do not omit the 'Against our common enemies' clause from the first article, the material clause of the 2nd article ('Without respect of persons, endeavor the extirpation...'), the 3rd and 4th articles, the justice clause in the 5th article, the entirety of the 6th article, or the material paragraph of the conclusion. Leaving these out is evidence that a proposed 'renovation' is not a true renewal but a new, deceitful bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve civil obligations in covenant bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: Covenant renewals and bonds must retain the civil as well as religious duties originally included; the civil part cannot be lawfully omitted under pretense of avoiding a 'blending' of civil and religious matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Presbytery rejects the excuse that including civil obligations is an improper blending; the covenants historically included civil duties and magistrates as lawful objects, and omitting them constitutes a betrayal of the covenants' purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: No relaxation of former obligations by new bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: A people may by a new bond add obligations but cannot, without guilt, relax, cancel, or withdraw former obligations previously sworn to God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle drawn from history: Ancestors who renewed covenants always included prior obligations and went further, never rescinded former vows. A 'renovation' that pares off prior obligations is equated with perjury and deceit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renovation must advance not retreat
rubrics_metrics.description: Renovation of covenants should follow the example of reformers who advanced reformation; it should not go back to earlier forms that omit later improvements or condemn previous reforming steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Returning to older covenant forms (e.g., 1580/1581) while ignoring the developments and explicit condemnations (e.g., of Prelacy) that later renewals (1638/1648) made explicit. Such step-backwards are portrayed as burying the work of reformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and unbiased testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: A faithful testimony for reformation must be even-handed, condemning corruptions in both church and state as appropriate, and must embody the full historical testimony of the covenanted church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Presbytery criticizes the Seceders' Act and Testimony as principally leveled only against church judicatories while being silent or flattering regarding the civil usurpations (Erastianism). A faithful testimony should 'charge home' sins across ranks to effect conviction and repentance rather than flatter rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit denunciation of civil usurpation (Erastianism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where civil power has usurped ecclesiastical authority, a faithful testimony must explicitly denounce that usurpation rather than obscure or flatter civil sovereigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Praising the king as 'the best of kings' or failing to name the civil usurper when the revolution constitution has involved the nation in 'guilt of apostasy'. The Presbytery expects candid rebuke ('Thou art the man') where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of ministerial and Christian communion must be just and charitable
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms imposed for ministerial license, ordination, or admission to the Lord's supper must not be unwarrantably restrictive or exclude faithful persons who conscientiously cannot accept novel or deceitful conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of abuse: forcing public renunciations before license, rejecting honest accessions until they drop former testimonies, or making adherence to an 'artificial bond' a requirement for Christian communion. Such restrictions are 'partly destructive' of Christian liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid imposing political tests for ministry
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates for license or ordination should not be compelled to adopt or maintain party-political principles (e.g., anti-government schemes) as prerequisites for ministry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific instance: adding a question asking candidates whether they will adhere to the Associate Presbytery's political answers is improper. Binding new ministers to an 'anti-government scheme' undermines the church's integrity and renders ministry conditional on political conformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacramental admission must follow scriptural qualifications, not political loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications for worthy receivers of the Lord's supper must be biblical and spiritual, not theological or political loyalty to civil rulers or current constitutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Presbytery objects to making 'subjection and loyalty' to an Erastian authority a commendatory qualification for the Lord's supper. This conflates civil obedience with sacramental worthiness and is condemned as absurd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church discipline must observe scriptural formalities and justice
rubrics_metrics.description: When exercising censures (e.g., excommunication), church courts must use the formalities, means of conviction, and common justice required by Scripture and the church's standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns cited: proceeding to excommunication without required formalities, sentencing without due process, or exercising arbitrary tyranny ('pretended libel') against ministers and elders who uphold covenantal principles. Such abuses render courts unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful constitution and powers of church courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicatories claiming parity of power or acting beyond their scriptural constitution are not lawful courts of Christ and should not be countenanced or submitted to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Presbytery declares the Associate Presbytery/Synod, claiming parity, to be not lawful or rightly constituted according to Scripture and historical Presbyterian testimony. Courts must be consistent with the Word and the church's covenanted standards.
